title: Incident scope decision tree and evidence collection playbook
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Overview

This playbook defines a deterministic decision tree to scope security incidents and a prioritized, evidence-first collection process that spans RBAC/auth artifacts, audit logs, model-serving telemetry, data residency concerns, and secure-SDLC triggers. It is intended for the Security Incident Lead (SIL), oncall SREs, and the forensic engineers who will assemble compliance evidence for audits and legal review.

Goals
- Determine incident scope within 30 minutes of triage start.
- Collect preserved evidence within 2 hours for high-severity incidents (P0/P1).
- Produce a compliance evidence bundle within 48 hours when required by legal or regional data-residency constraints.

Audience and ownership
- Primary owner: security (Incident Response).
- Secondary owners: eng-sre (log access), eng-serving-runtime (model telemetry), eng-private-deployments (data residency triggers).
- SIL responsibilities: run the decision tree, authorize containment actions, sign off on evidence handoff.

Decision tree (high-level)
1) Confirm detection source
   - Is the alert from an internal monitoring system (tracing/alerts/console) or an external report (customer/legal/regulator)?
   - If external, mark as candidate for restricted evidence packaging and notify Legal.
2) Rapid impact assessment (R0 - R3)
   - R0: Confirmed data exfiltration of customer PII or model weights.
   - R1: Suspicious authentication events or privilege escalations.
   - R2: System instability or degraded components without evidence of compromise.
   - R3: Informational or false-positive.
3) Residency and compliance flags
   - Does affected data fall under geo-residency or contractual restrictions? (EU/UK/CAN/Customer VPC).
   - If yes, escalate to Data Residency Owner and restrict exportable artifacts.
4) Evidence tiering decision
   - If R0 or R1 -> Tier A evidence collection (full forensic capture).
   - If R2 -> Tier B evidence (targeted logs + configuration snapshots).
   - If R3 -> Tier C (summary + monitoring retention).

Prioritized evidence collection checklist (Tier A / high-severity)
1) Snapshot and isolate:
   - Create immutable VM/container snapshots of affected hosts (note storage location and hash).
   - For managed GPU inference pods, snapshot the model-serving node and preserve KV-cache dumps where possible.
2) Access & RBAC artifacts (Collect first)
   - Identity events: authentication logs, MFA failures, JIT privilege activations, and service account tokens issued (last 7 days).
   - Group and role changes: audit entries showing role bindings, entitlement grants, and approval artifacts.
   - Active sessions: list of current sessions, open sockets, and process owners.
3) Audit logging (Collect second, but preserve early)
   - Ingestion: preserve raw audit streams for the incident window (+30 minutes before detection).
   - Relevant tables/indices: index names, schema versions, retention policies.\   - Query examples (CLI):
     # preserve index snapshot (Elasticsearch example)
     curl -XPOST "https://es.local/_snapshot/forensic_repo/snap1/_create?wait_for_completion=true" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"indices":"audit-*,auth-*,serving-*","ignore_unavailable":true}'
4) Telemetry and model-serving traces (Collect third)
   - Per-request traces for model endpoints: request id, model variant, sequence length, token counts.
   - Cache/KV artifacts and batching metadata.
5) Data residency-sensitive artifacts
   - If data is geo-fenced, collect metadata only and escalate for legal approval before exporting full payloads.
   - Maintain a redaction manifest for PII before any cross-region transfer.
6) Build and SDLC artifacts (Collect last)
   - Recent CI/CD pipeline runs, release tags, deployment approvals, and dependency manifests that could have introduced the change.

Roles and responsibilities matrix
| Role | Immediate action | Evidence ownership | Escalation |
| SIL (Security Incident Lead) | Run tree, set severity, approve Tier | Approves evidence package | Legal, CTO, Customer-commit owner |
| Forensic Engineer | Execute collection checklists, hash manifests | Stores immutable artifacts in forensic store | SIL |
| Oncall SRE | Provide snapshots, network captures, and shift logs | Live system telemetry collection | Forensic Engineer |
| Data Residency Owner | Approve cross-border exports, advise redaction | Manages residency flags and manifests | Legal |

Minimum artifact manifest (required for Tier A)
- incident-id: string (human and UUID)
- collection-time-window: string (UTC start/end)
- collectors: list of names and emails
- artifact-list: list of artifact identifiers and SHA256 hashes
- redaction-manifest: list of fields redacted and reason

Example manifest (JSON snippet - for clarity only):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0458",
  "window": "2026-02-28T16:12:00Z/2026-02-28T18:30:00Z",
  "collectors": ["lena.ortiz@redwood.ai", "marcos.lee@redwood.ai"],
  "artifacts": [
    {"id":"auth-events-20260228-1","sha256":"e3b0c442..."},
    {"id":"es-snapshot-20260228-1","sha256":"af12b9..."}
  ]
}

Evidence packaging SLOs and retention guidance
- Tier A: package produced within 48 hours; forensic retention 7 years (or contract-specified).
- Tier B: package produced within 7 days; retention 2 years.
- Tier C: incident summary in the incident log within 48 hours; follow standard retention.

Chain-of-custody and attestations
1) Every collector signs the manifest with an HMAC using their SSO private key and stores the signature in the evidence store.
2) For restricted/data residency incidents, Legal must sign the export authorization before any artifact leaves the region.
3) All handoffs must be recorded in the incident timeline (UTC timestamped) with actor and reason.

Special procedures by subsystem
- RBAC & Auth: preserve identity provider logs (OIDC provider audit, SCIM provisioning, IAM change approvals). If service accounts are implicated, rotate keys after snapshotting and log the rotation event as part of the manifest.
- Audit logging: do not reindex or transform raw logs prior to snapshot. If redaction is required, keep original checksums and store redacted copies separately.
- Data residency: if affected tenant data is located in a customer-managed VPC or a jurisdiction with legal hold, follow the Private Deployments evidence export checklist before any cross-boundary transfer.
- Secure SDLC: snapshot the exact CI artifact (container digest, commit SHA, build metadata). If a deployment approval bypass is suspected, include the pipeline run and approval token history.

Communication and escalation steps
1) SIL sets an internal comms channel (private incident room) with a documented retention and membership.
2) Notify Legal and Privacy for Tier A incidents and request export authorization early.
3) If a customer is affected, follow the Customer Communication SOP (product-docs) and obtain Legal/CS approval before external disclosure.

Query recipes and utilities (examples)
- Find all auth failures for a user in the window (Clickhouse example):
  SELECT * FROM auth_events WHERE user_id = 'alice@example.com' AND event_time BETWEEN toDateTime('2026-02-28 16:00:00') AND toDateTime('2026-02-28 18:30:00') AND result = 'FAIL'
- Capture open network connections on a host (linux):
  sudo ss -tupan > /forensic/INC-2026-XXXX/ss-connections.txt

Table: Recommended artifact retention by category
| Artifact category | Recommended retention | Export constraints |
| audit logs (raw) | 3 years (min); 7 years preferred for regulated customers | Export only after Legal approval for cross-border |
| RBAC change history | 7 years | Redaction allowed for PII identifiers in some regions |
| Model-serving traces | 1 year default; extend to 3 years for regulated customers | Sensitive request payloads require redaction |
| Build and CI artifacts | 2 years | No export constraints unless containing customer secrets |

Post-incident review and evidence disposition
- Within 10 business days, Security and Forensics produce an Evidence Disposition memo listing what was archived, what was returned to live systems, and any data destroyed per legal direction.
- Retention exceptions must be filed in the Risk Exceptions tracker with owner, justification, and expiration date.

Appendix A — Quick checklist (first 2 hours)
1) SIL: classify severity and set incident id.
2) Forensic Engineer: start VM/container snapshots and collect RBAC artifacts.
3) Oncall SRE: preserve audit index snapshot and provide query endpoints.
4) Data Residency Owner: flag any geo-sensitive payloads and approve manifest redaction plan.
5) Legal: if notified, confirm whether export is permitted and request embargo if required.
